headline: SK Group will pay about 50 people aged 19 to 34 roughly $2,200 a month for two years to learn to use AI on real problems, with no degree or job promised.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a concrete education offer with money attached, but small (about 50 places) and a single company's program.
importance_line: What changed is that a major Korean company will fund young people to learn AI through projects rather than a degree, which gives about 50 people aged 19 to 34 a paid path first, then universities and employers watching a different route into AI work, but the program is small and promises no job.
summary: The Korea Times reports that SK Group, a large South Korean conglomerate, said on Monday 12 Oct 2026 it will launch SK AIGEN, a two-year, full-time, non-degree program starting in March 2027 for about 50 people aged 19 to 34, paying a monthly stipend of 3 million won (about $2,200). Run by SK's in-house training platform mySUNI, it guarantees neither a job nor a degree and will pick applicants on their willingness to solve problems rather than academic background, with applications open from 1 to 15 Nov.
notes: Full text read. SK's announcement as reported by The Korea Times; no independent confirmation read.
